options_evaluated: Glass-fiber reinforced polyamide (PA66-GF30) with overmolded TPE grips
Unreinforced recycled Polycarbonate/ABS (PC/ABS) blend with mechanically fastened TPU grips
Cast aluminum alloy housing with silicone sleeves
decisions.conflict: Overmolding TPE grips onto a PA66-GF30 housing optimizes structural strength and manufacturing cycle times but permanently bonds dissimilar polymers, preventing clean material separation and high-value recycling at end-of-life.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (t), page 80: lightweight design as expressed through reduction of material consumption, use of lower density or high-strength materials
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, as expressed through number of materials and components used
decisions.chief_resolution: Select the unreinforced recycled PC/ABS blend with mechanically fastened TPU grips. This design avoids co-molding or chemically bonding dissimilar plastics, facilitating clean mechanical disassembly and sorting at end-of-life, while utilizing recycled content to minimize the material footprint.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the supply chain availability of high-purity post-consumer recycled PC/ABS resins in the EU and verify that the mechanical snap-fit tolerances can accommodate recycled material shrinkage variations.

options_evaluated: Threaded fasteners (Torx screws) with brass heat-stake inserts
decisions.conflict: Ultrasonic welding minimizes assembly costs and part count but creates a permanent joint that prevents non-destructive disassembly, rendering the internal components unrepairable.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly, and compatibility with commonly available tools
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c), page 79: ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment as expressed through ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly
decisions.chief_resolution: Recommend threaded fasteners (standardized Torx screws) paired with brass heat-stake inserts. This mechanical fastening strategy ensures that the housing can be repeatedly disassembled and re-assembled without degrading the plastic threads, allowing non-destructive access to internal components for repair.
decisions.design_action: Verify the availability of standardized Torx fastener sizes across the entire tool assembly to ensure compatibility with commonly available consumer toolsets.

options_evaluated: Brushed DC motor with copper commutator
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with neodymium magnets
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with ferrite magnets
decisions.conflict: Neodymium-based BLDC motors provide superior energy efficiency and power-to-weight ratios during use but rely heavily on critical raw materials that are difficult to recover and recycle at end-of-life.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components as expressed through technical lifetime, mean time between failures
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (h), page 79: use or content of recycled materials and recovery of materials, including critical raw materials
decisions.chief_resolution: Select a high-efficiency Brushless DC (BLDC) motor optimized to minimize neodymium content or utilize ferrite magnets. This choice dramatically extends the technical lifetime and reliability of the tool compared to brushed motors while reducing reliance on critical raw materials.
decisions.design_action: Investigate motor supplier specifications to check the minimum weight of rare-earth elements required and assess the feasibility of a modular rotor design that allows easy extraction of the magnets prior to shredding.

options_evaluated: Active cooling with an integrated plastic fan on the motor shaft
Passive cooling via cast aluminum internal heat sinks
Phase-change material (PCM) encapsulation around the motor housing
decisions.conflict: Encapsulating the motor in phase-change materials significantly improves thermal stability and extends motor life but introduces complex chemical mixtures that complicate material recovery and recycling.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (f), page 79: use of substances, and in particular the use of substances of concern, leading to their presence in products, including once those products become waste
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: resistance to stresses or ageing mechanisms
decisions.chief_resolution: Implement passive cooling via a structural, cast aluminum internal heat sink that is mechanically separable from the motor. This avoids the introduction of chemical substances of concern or complex mixtures while ensuring adequate resistance to thermal stress and ageing.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the assembly stack-up to verify that the aluminum heat sink can be slid out or detached without damaging the motor or housing, ensuring clean separation of aluminum and copper.

options_evaluated: Monolithic internal chassis with integrated motor, gearbox, and electronics
Modular architecture with separate slide-in modules for motor, gearbox, and trigger/switch assembly
Fully potted electronics assembly for environmental sealing
decisions.conflict: A monolithic chassis reduces assembly complexity and manufacturing cost but forces the replacement of the entire drive assembly if only a single component (like the trigger switch) fails.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, as expressed through modularity, compatibility with commonly available tools and spare parts
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e), page 79: avoidance of technical solutions detrimental to reuse, upgrading, repair, maintenance, refurbishment
decisions.chief_resolution: Implement a modular architecture with separate slide-in modules for the motor/gearbox and the switch assembly. This directly supports Annex I (b) and (e) by allowing targeted replacement of high-wear components without discarding functioning parts.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the physical and electrical interface standards (e.g., plug-and-play wire harnesses instead of soldered joints) to verify that modules can be replaced independently by a consumer or professional repairer.

options_evaluated: Removable and standardized slide-on Lithium-Ion battery pack
decisions.conflict: An integrated, soldered cell pack allows for a more compact, lightweight product design but prevents easy battery replacement, leading to premature product disposal when the cells degrade.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, as expressed through modularity, ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability as expressed through technical lifetime, resistance to stresses or ageing mechanisms
decisions.chief_resolution: Recommend a removable and standardized slide-on Lithium-Ion battery pack. This ensures the battery (the component most susceptible to capacity degradation over time) can be easily replaced, significantly extending the technical lifetime of the tool and facilitating safe end-of-life recycling.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the compatibility of the battery interface with existing cross-brand battery alliances (e.g., CAS or Power for All) to verify if a standardized battery platform can be adopted.
